selected_mechanism.name: DAF Enhanced-Use-Lease Source Selection for Commercial AI Data Centers at JBER, Eielson AFB & Clear SFS (AFCEC-26-R-0006)
selected_mechanism.one_line_definition: The Air Force is using 10 U.S.C. 2667 Enhanced Use Lease authority to competitively outlease ~4,700 acres across three Alaska installations to a single private developer who finances, permits, powers, builds, and operates commercial AI data centers on-base while the government keeps title and collects fair-market rent, with a federal source-selection board, not the Alaska grid or state land, deciding who wins.

news_trigger.verbatim_quote: Responses to the Air Force's Request for Lease Proposals are due by June 29.

layers.layer_name: Statutory outlease authority (10 U.S.C. 2667 Enhanced Use Lease)
layers.what_it_does: Lets the DAF lease non-excess, underutilized on-base property (~4,700 acres across JBER, Eielson AFB, Clear SFS) to a commercial partner for long-term use while retaining title and collecting fair-market consideration.
layers.controlling_actor: Secretary of the Air Force (delegated), executed via the DAF/AFCEC Enhanced Use Lease program
layers.source_note: Official af.mil release confirms 'Under the Enhanced Use Lease model, the service leases non-excess property to partners for long-term commercial use' and the ~4,700 acres across the three named Alaska installations.

layers.what_it_does: Runs the competitive Request for Lease Proposals, evaluates offers on a best-value basis, and decides whether to enter lease negotiations with an offeror. Offer close June 29, 2026 (extended from May 29); now in non-public source selection.
layers.controlling_actor: Air Force Installation Contracting Agency (AFICA); Contracting Officer Julia A. Cantrell
layers.source_note: SAM.gov solicitation mirror confirms solicitation AFCEC-26-R-0006, contracting agency AFICA, POC Julia A. Cantrell, response due June 29, 2026, for 'development of commercial Artificial Intelligence (AI) data centers' at the three Alaska sites.

layers.layer_name: Utility-accessibility requirement embedded in the RFLP
layers.what_it_does: Forces each offeror to self-solve firm power, water, and bandwidth. The RFLP requires offerors to demonstrate how they minimize impacts to community access, affordability, reliability, and quality of energy, exporting Railbelt power risk onto the lessee rather than the government.
layers.controlling_actor: Offeror as risk-bearer; Golden Valley Electric Association (GVEA) as prospective interconnecting utility (recommended 138-kV connection, capacity not yet assessed)
layers.source_note: Quotes the RFLP: DAF 'is requiring offerors to demonstrate in their proposals how they would minimize and mitigate impacts and risk to the surrounding community, specifically related to the access to and affordability, reliability, and quality of energy, water, and communication bandwidth.' News-Miner separately confirms the RFLP notes GVEA recommended 138-kV connection but 'would need to assess actual capacity', correcting the scout's overstated 'GVEA can't support' framing.

layers.what_it_does: The winning commercial partner finances, permits, builds, powers, and operates the AI data centers on-base; government may separately purchase services if desired. Identity not public as of 2026-07-08 (in source selection).
layers.controlling_actor: To-be-selected commercial developer (institutional lessee role; identity pending award)
layers.source_note: af.mil release confirms the EUL partner develops/operates commercial data centers on leased land; award recipient not yet named, which is why the mechanism (not the actor) is the story.

chokepoint.actor: AFICA Contracting Officer / Source Selection Authority (currently CO Julia A. Cantrell)
chokepoint.binary_decision: Enter lease negotiations with an offeror or not, a single best-value determination by one federal contracting desk that gates who, if anyone, gets to build developer-financed AI data centers on Alaska bases.
chokepoint.why_asymmetric: One officer/source-selection authority owns the go/no-go on the EUL award; it is not a shared committee vote. The competing 'facilities' framing (GVEA board + RCA tariff approval) is a multi-actor committee and, per the overlap rule, loses to this single-desk chokepoint. Power is not a separate veto here, the RFLP folds it into the offeror's own burden of proof, which the same AFICA board scores.

ak_consequence.sector: AI data-center infrastructure and Railbelt power
ak_consequence.stake: Whether Interior/Southcentral Alaska captures a large developer-financed on-base AI data-center build turns on the AFICA best-value determination now underway; a proposal that cannot demonstrate bankable firm power fails the RFLP's utility-accessibility test regardless of capital, likely concentrating any award at JBER on the Chugach system rather than Eielson on GVEA's 138-kV line.
ak_consequence.named_actor: AFICA (CO Julia A. Cantrell) as source-selection gate; GVEA as prospective Fairbanks interconnector; to-be-named developer
ak_consequence.timeframe: Non-public source selection now; lease negotiations / award decision H2 2026.

selected_mechanism.structural_read: This is a procurement vehicle, not a real-estate story. The Air Force has structured the deal so that a single federal source-selection board, not Alaska's grid operators, not ADNR, not the RCA, decides whether Alaska gets a hyperscale AI build, and it has deliberately pushed the hardest Alaska-specific constraint (firm, affordable dispatchable power on a capacity-uncertain Railbelt) onto the private lessee as a scored evaluation factor. The government keeps title and collects rent; the developer eats the power risk. That inversion is the mechanism: it makes the AFICA best-value tradeoff the real chokepoint and turns bankable power into the pass/fail variable inside it.
selected_mechanism.forward_implication: Source selection is closed to the public; the next observable event is a lease-negotiation or award announcement in H2 2026. An allocator or developer positioning for Alaska AI infrastructure should track which offeror can evidence firm dispatchable power, on-site generation versus a GVEA 138-kV interconnection whose capacity is unproven, because that single factor, scored by AFICA, likely determines whether the award lands at Eielson (GVEA) or defaults to JBER (Chugach).

dropped_mechanisms.name: SBA 8(a) Entity-Owned Eligibility & Enforcement Machinery (ANC federal-contracting carve-out)
dropped_mechanisms.reason: Passes news_tie (June 11 rule, comment period closes July 13) and is a genuine fresh chokepoint, but edged out and marginal: load-bearing enforcement/freeze layers rest on trade reporting, and the Alaska-AI consequence is indirect. Strongest fresh alternative for next cycle once its enforcement/freeze layers can be pinned to a primary docket.

dropped_mechanisms.name: FCC Submarine Cable Landing License national-security review regime (FCC 25-49 / Second R&O)
dropped_mechanisms.reason: News tie verified (Federal Register 91 FR 42137, effective 2026-07-08) but fails chokepoint asymmetry: Team Telecom is a DOJ-chaired multi-agency committee, not one desk. Non-FCC layers under-sourced and the Alaska nexus is not established in the triggering document (confabulation risk).

dropped_mechanisms.name: Alaska Railbelt large-load (data-center) interconnection standards (RCA/RRC gap)
dropped_mechanisms.reason: News hook is a national FERC Section 206 action aimed at the six Lower-48 RTOs/ISOs, Alaska explicitly outside it, so no discrete in-window Alaska trigger; RRC-FAC standards in progress, not a dated order; RCA/utility layers could not be primary-sourced (403s).

_validation_note: Selected the DAF EUL AI data-center mechanism because it clears all seven points with primary sources fetched and confirmed: af.mil (10 U.S.C. 2667 EUL model + 4,700 acres/three installations), the SAM.gov solicitation mirror (AFCEC-26-R-0006, AFICA, CO Julia A. Cantrell, June 29 offer close), and RFLP text quoted in News-Miner and Alaska's News Source. OVERLAP RULE applied: trigger surfaced from both the vehicles and facilities scouts; took the vehicles framing (AFICA source selection = one contracting officer's go/no-go) as the sharper single-desk chokepoint over the facilities multi-actor committee framing (GVEA board + RCA tariff). Verification caught paraphrase drift in the facilities framing: the scout's 'GVEA has said it currently can't support a large data center' is not supported; News-Miner states GVEA did not respond and the RFLP records GVEA recommending a 138-kV connection subject to a capacity assessment; corrected in the layer note. THEMATIC-FATIGUE: third consecutive data-center/power mechanism after ADNR state-land and Railbelt LNG, but clears point 7 on mechanism grounds (federal 10 U.S.C. 2667 outlease with a federal source-selection chokepoint is structurally different from state land disposal or Railbelt gas supply). Window NOT broadened; all sourcing within 14 days. Mapper suffered three transient 529 API overloads before a fresh spawn completed the gate; orchestrator applied the transient-error retry rule (no facts changed by the retries).
